digest.component_or_area: store write path (event_commit_git, txn claim/transition, delete, compact, fsck)
propositions: Lock-held git commit on a mature store exceeds the 30s per-commit timeout when git >=2.47 runs foreground auto-maintenance (repack) inside the commit subprocess, causing SIGKILL mid-write and data loss.

The 30s bound was copied from the network push path and is incorrect for local lock-held commits that carry O(store) maintenance work; the operator explicitly rejected raising the timeout as masking the root cause.

Suppressing auto-maintenance on the commit via -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false makes the bounded commit O(1), then replaying git maintenance run --auto as a deferred step under the same lock on the 120s watchdog bound preserves ADR 0051 serialization while decoupling repack from the tight commit latency bound.
All lock-held store-commit surfaces must be covered: event_append primary + recovery commits, txn claim/transition, delete, compact_plan, compact ticket-compact-all, and fsck_repair batch commits.
Regression test confirms write succeeds (does not timeout and lose data) when foreground maintenance is suppressed and deferred, falsifying rivals (lock contention, network cost, code regression).
The fix removes the SIGKILL-mid-repack corruption hazard that violates ADR 0051 while keeping the 30s bound and c2ba parity test intact.
